note: `AbortController` and `AbortSignal` with `abort(reason)`, `AbortSignal.abort()`, `timeout()` and `any()`. The `signal` option of `addEventListener` removes the listener on abort, both on nodes and on other event targets. With `Runtime.node()`, `fetch` and Node's own APIs take a signal too.
No device sensor APIs.
No device sensor APIs.

`readText()`, `writeText()`, `read()`, `write()` and `ClipboardItem` work on the system clipboard for `text/plain`, `text/html` and `image/png`, the types `ClipboardItem.supports()` names. A write takes one item, as in Chromium.
No audio output or Web Audio API.
There is no `auxclick` event; `pointerdown` and `pointerup` carry `button` for every button.
A service worker feature for pages that sync while closed.

`navigator.getBattery()` resolves to a `BatteryManager` with `charging`, `level`, `chargingTime` and `dischargingTime`, read from the system: IOKit on macOS, `/sys/class/power_supply` on Linux and `GetSystemPowerStatus` on Windows. With no battery to read, it reports a full battery on external power, as the spec allows. The change events come from a re-read every 30 seconds while something listens. Apps on `Runtime.node()` do not have it yet. Silk apps read the same values with `ui_tree.battery.read()`.
`sendBeacon` sends data as a page unloads; an app can send it with `fetch` before it quits.
Printing events are about printing documents.
The default engine runtime's `Blob` has no `stream()`.
Only with `App.runtime(Runtime.node())`, the SilkJS runtime; the default engine runtime has no `URL.createObjectURL`.
Only with `App.runtime(Runtime.node())`, the SilkJS runtime; the default engine runtime has no `BroadcastChannel`.
Only with `App.runtime(Runtime.node())`, the SilkJS runtime; the default engine runtime has no `MessageChannel`.

`copy`, `cut` and `paste` fire at the focused node from the shortcuts, the Edit menu and the input context menu, and bubble. `clipboardData` is a `DataTransfer`: a prevented copy or cut writes what a listener set, and a paste carries `text/plain`, `text/html` and a pasted PNG in `files`. Cut and paste edits fire `beforeinput` (`deleteByCut`, `insertFromPaste`) first, and preventing it cancels the edit.
Lines go to the host's standard error.
`console.time`, `timeLog`, `timeEnd`, `count`, `countReset`, `group` and `groupEnd` work; `console.table` prints its argument as `console.log` does.

Form controls and `<form>` implement `ValidityState`, `willValidate`, `validity`, `validationMessage`, `setCustomValidity()`, `checkValidity()`, `reportValidity()`, `invalid` events, and `:valid` / `:invalid` / `:user-valid` / `:user-invalid`.
Cookies belong to pages in a browser.
CORS restricts what pages may fetch from other origins; an app's requests are not under the same-origin policy.
No `createImageBitmap`.
No `navigator.credentials`.
Only with `App.runtime(Runtime.node())`, the SilkJS runtime; the default engine runtime has no `crypto.subtle`.

`CSS.supports(property, value)` and `CSS.supports(conditionText)`, with `selector()`, answered by the same parser as a stylesheet's `@supports`. `font-tech()` and `font-format()` answer false, as they do in `@supports`.
`CustomEvent`, `Event` and `EventTarget` work, and nodes take listeners for event types of the app's own: `node.dispatchEvent(event)` sends one through the tree with a capture and a bubble phase.
No device orientation or motion events.
A browser privacy setting for websites.
There is no document or `<script>` element.
XPath queries a document; a Silk UI app has a tree of nodes, not a document.
A deprecated API for editable documents. Rich inputs have `format()` and `toggleMark()` for the same job.

`Range`, `StaticRange` and `createRange()` follow the DOM Standard over the app's nodes, and live ranges follow every change; they match Chromium on the WPT-style cases in `modules/js/packages/core/test/ranges`. `getClientRects()` and `getBoundingClientRect()` read the tree's layout. Without a `document`, `document.createRange()` is `createRange()` from `@silkui/core`.

`scrollTo`, `scroll` and `scrollBy` take `(x, y)` or `{ left, top, behavior }`. `behavior: "smooth"` animates in the tree only while the scroll moves, and `auto` follows the node's `scroll-behavior`. `scrollLeft` and `scrollTop` can be set.
No media playback, so no encrypted media either.
No `EventSource` in either runtime; with `App.runtime(Runtime.node())`, read the stream with `fetch`.
A header for pages and their frames.
Only with `App.runtime(Runtime.node())`, the SilkJS runtime; the default engine runtime has no `fetch`.

`File` and `Blob` read their bytes with `text()`, `arrayBuffer()` and `bytes()`, and `FormData` holds strings and files. Files dropped on a window arrive as `File`-like objects with a `name` and a `path`, read through `node:fs` with `App.runtime(Runtime.node())` and `App.allow(Access.Files)`. No `FileReader` in the default runtime.
Only with `App.runtime(Runtime.node())`, the SilkJS runtime; the default engine runtime has no `FileReader`.
No workers, and no `FileReaderSync`.
A deprecated sandboxed file system for pages. With `App.runtime(Runtime.node())` and `App.allow(Access.Files)`, use `node:fs`.
No Gamepad API.
No `navigator.geolocation`.

`getBoundingClientRect()`, `getClientRects()`, the `client*`, `scroll*` and `offset*` metrics, `elementFromPoint`, `elementsFromPoint` and `caretPositionFromPoint` read the tree, laying out first only when something changed. Silk code reads the same through `ui_tree.cssom_view`.
`crypto.getRandomValues` and `crypto.randomUUID` take their bits from the operating system. `crypto.subtle` is there only with `App.runtime(Runtime.node())`.
No device sensor APIs.
About the address of a page. `@silkui/foldkit` keeps an address in memory for its router.
`performance.now()` runs on the host's clock, and `performance.timeOrigin` is the wall-clock time it counts from.
No camera access.
IME composition works in inputs, but there is no API to read or steer the IME from script.
No IndexedDB in either runtime. With `App.runtime(Runtime.node())` and `App.allow(Access.Files)`, keep data in files with `node:fs`.
No IndexedDB in either runtime.
No file or directory picker yet; files can be dropped on a window.
Silk UI has no HTML. Nodes are made with `createBox` and `createText`, or by a framework.

Computed in the tree after each layout and scroll, clipped through every scroll container and `overflow` clip, with `root`, `rootMargin` and `threshold` lists. Callbacks run only when a target crosses a threshold. The parent chain stands for the containing block chain, so a fixed box inside a scroller is still clipped by it.
`scrollMargin` works. `trackVisibility` and `delay` are there but `isVisible` is always false.
No device sensor APIs.

Nodes have `matches()`, `webkitMatchesSelector()`, `closest()`, `querySelector()` and `querySelectorAll()` (a static array), run by the selector matcher that stylesheets use, so they agree with CSS, including live states and `:has()`. An invalid selector throws a `SyntaxError`. A browser (web canvas) build has no tree to ask, so they find nothing there. `@silkui/foldkit`'s elements keep their own simpler matcher for HTML tag names.

`matchMedia` answers any media query for the window, including `resolution`, the viewport size and the host's appearance and motion preferences. Lists with a `change` listener or `onchange` hear when the answer flips, for example when the window moves to a display of another scale.
Inputs have no length limit attribute; cut the value in an `input` listener.
No media capture.
No media capture or recording.
No media playback.
No Web MIDI.
No `MutationObserver`. The app makes every change to its nodes itself.
No `localStorage` or `sessionStorage` in either runtime. With `App.runtime(Runtime.node())` and `App.allow(Access.Files)`, keep data in a file with `node:fs`.
No file pickers. With `App.runtime(Runtime.node())` and `App.allow(Access.Files)`, `node:fs` reads and writes any file the app may.
Times the loading of a page.
No `navigator.connection`.

Importing `@silkui/core` gives `Notification`: `new Notification(title, { body })` shows a desktop notification, with `click` and `show` events. Permission is always granted; `close()`, icons and actions do nothing.
No real-time communication APIs.
No `navigator.onLine` or `online` and `offline` events.
No device sensor APIs.
About pages entering and leaving a browser's history.
Script cannot ask whether the window is visible or minimized.
No WebAuthn or passkeys.
Browser checkout for shopping pages.
No `navigator.permissions`.
A header for pages and their frames.
No picture-in-picture windows.
No pointer lock.
Embeds and navigates between pages.
No device sensor APIs.
Server pushes to a page's service worker. An app can hold its own connection, with `WebSocket` under `App.runtime(Runtime.node())`.
Callbacks run before the window's frames, with the frame time.
`requestIdleCallback` runs the callback from a timer, with a 50 ms `timeRemaining()` budget; the `timeout` option changes nothing, since the callback never waits longer than a timer.

Entries carry `contentRect`, `borderBoxSize`, `contentBoxSize` and `devicePixelContentBoxSize`, after a layout that changed the observed box and before paint. A change a callback makes is laid out in the next frame.
Times the resources a page loads.
No WebRTC.
No `screen.orientation`.
`true`, `false` or `{ block, inline, behavior }`, through every scroll container, with `scroll-margin`, `scroll-padding` and snapping.
Scrolls only the containers that do not already show the node, centered unless `centerIfNeeded` is false.

`getSelection()` is the selection the user makes in the app's text, with Chrome's rules, and scripts can read and change it: `addRange`, `collapse`, `extend`, `setBaseAndExtent`, `selectAllChildren`, `containsNode`, `deleteFromDocument` and the rest, over live ranges. `toString()` gives the text as copying does. `selectstart` (cancelable) and `selectionchange` reach listeners; the document's `selectionchange` fires at the mounted root. Not there: `modify()`, and inputs keep their own selection (`selectionStart`, `setSelectionRange`) rather than showing in `getSelection()`. Across children that layout reorders, the selection holds one range per piece seen.
Reports server timings of a page's requests to its devtools.
Service workers make pages work offline; an app is offline already.
Shared workers share one worker between pages.
No speech recognition.
No speech synthesis. To have a screen reader speak, use `announce()` from `@silkui/core`.
Web SQL is deprecated and gone from browsers.
No camera or microphone access.
Only with `App.runtime(Runtime.node())`, the SilkJS runtime; the default engine runtime has no `ReadableStream`, `WritableStream` or `TransformStream`.
`TextDecoder` reads UTF-8, UTF-16 and windows-1252 (`latin1`); other labels throw a `RangeError`.

`touchstart`, `touchmove`, `touchend` and `touchcancel` with `touches`, `targetTouches` and `changedTouches`, after each finger's pointer events and before a tap's mouse events, as in Chrome. A touch stays with the node it went down on, and preventing `touchstart` or the first `touchmove` stops the pan and the tap's click. Fingers come from Windows, macOS, Wayland and the browser. No host reports `force` or `radiusX`/`radiusY` yet, and `touches` lists only fingers on nodes with touch listeners.
Guards HTML injection into a document; Silk UI has no HTML.
A deprecated API, replaced by WebAuthn.
Only with `App.runtime(Runtime.node())`, the SilkJS runtime; the default engine runtime has no `URL`.
Only with `App.runtime(Runtime.node())`, the SilkJS runtime; the default engine runtime has no `URLSearchParams`.
`performance.mark`, `measure`, `getEntries`, `getEntriesByName`, `getEntriesByType`, `clearMarks` and `clearMeasures` work. The default runtime has no `PerformanceObserver`.
No `navigator.vibrate`.
No screen wake lock.
No `element.animate()`. CSS transitions and `@keyframes` animations work through styles.
No Bluetooth access.
No serial port access.
No `navigator.share`.
No WebCodecs.
No WebGPU.
No HID device access.
No NFC access.
Only with `App.runtime(Runtime.node())`, the SilkJS runtime; the default engine runtime has no `WebSocket`.
No WebTransport.
No USB access.
Replaced by WebXR and gone from browsers.
No `Worker` in either runtime: an app's JavaScript runs on the UI thread.
No WebXR.
`postMessage` between pages and frames; an app has one realm.
No `XMLHttpRequest` in either runtime; `fetch` works with `App.runtime(Runtime.node())`.
Parses and serializes HTML and XML documents; Silk UI has no document.

`memoryUsage()` returns `{ footprint, processes }` in bytes: `phys_footprint` on macOS, `Pss` on Linux, `PrivateUsage` on Windows, the numbers Activity Monitor, `footprint` and Task Manager show. In a browser build it is only the wasm tree's memory.

`frameStats()` returns the frames the window presented since the last call, with presents per second, painted frames the GPU never drew, and the 50th, 95th and 99th percentile and longest milliseconds between presents. `null` in a browser build.
